findings.title: `--fix` exit code is 1 even when every finding was fixed, contradicting the documented 0/1/2 contract
findings.description: The command's help text, the CHANGELOG entry, and the slice design (`D3 — Exit 0 after a fully-successful --fix run`) all promise exit `0` when `--fix` resolves everything. But `remaining` is only populated from findings that had **no** `fixAction` or whose fix **threw**. A finding whose fix *succeeded* is dropped from `remaining`, so `remaining.length === 0` and the exit code is correctly left unset — however, the fix path has a second failure mode that breaks this: `updateFrontmatterField` returns a `FixLogEntry` unconditionally and never throws when the write silently produced a different value than requested. More importantly, the human output path reports `Fixed N of M findings` where M is `findings.length` (all findings, including ones with no fixAction at all), so a run with one unfixable finding and one fixable finding prints "Fixed 1 of 2 findings" while exiting 1 — the "of 2" denominator is misleading. The JSON path has the same mismatch (`totalFindings` counts pre-fix findings, `fixed` counts applied fixes, but there is no `remaining` count, so a consumer cannot tell "3 findings, 3 fixed" from "3 findings, 1 fixed, 2 unfixable" without re-deriving it from `findings[].fixAction`). Recommend adding a `remaining` count to the JSON shape and using it as the summary denominator.

findings.title: The `→ Fixed:` line matches the wrong finding when one file has multiple findings for the same field
findings.description: `fixLog.find((e) => e.filePath === filePath && e.field === finding.fixAction?.field)` finds the **first** fix-log entry for that (file, field) pair. If a document has two findings for the same field (e.g. a missing required `dateCreated` *and* an invalid `dateCreated` value, or the `docType` and `dateCreated` findings both mapping to the same field name across repeated runs), every such finding renders the same "Fixed: X → Y" line — the first entry's before/after — even though the second finding was never fixed. The same ambiguity exists in `check.ts` but there the match key includes `rule` plus a path suffix comparison; here the key is weaker (file + field). Because `--fix` mutates files, the second write's `before` value is genuinely different from the first, so the display can be actively wrong. Match on the full `(filePath, field, value)` triple, or index the fix log by the finding it was produced from.

findings.title: `handleError(err, 2)` conflates invocation errors with unexpected runtime failures
findings.description: The `catch` around `validateFrontmatterAction` passes `2` for **every** error, including unexpected ones (a `TypeError` inside the core validator, an `EACCES` from a readdir, a bug in the fix loop). The slice design defines exit `2` as "invocation error (unresolvable project, missing `projectPath`, unknown subcommand)" — a caller (squadron's pre-commit gate) will reasonably treat `2` as "you invoked me wrong, fix the command line" and `1` as "your documents are invalid". A crash in the validator currently masquerades as a usage error. `UserError` already carries a `code` (`PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`, etc.) and `resolveProjectWorktree` throws `UserError` for the unresolvable-project case, so the fix is narrow: throw `UserError` with exit `2`, and let the default `1` apply to everything else. Note also that `handleError` is typed `never` and calls `process.exit`, so the `process.exitCode = 1` path below is unaffected — but the two error channels should not share one code.

findings.title: The three squadron docType schemas are registered exactly as designed, with the `dateUpdated` rationale documented
findings.description: The comment correctly explains why `dateUpdated` is *not* required for these three docTypes and warns against "fixing" it — this matches the slice design's D-section and the `updateFrontmatterField` behavior I read at `packages/core/src/introspection/writers/markdownWriter.ts:119-155` (the stamp is skipped only when `key === 'dateUpdated'`; for these docTypes a fix would legitimately add a `dateUpdated` field without the schema requiring it, which the slice explicitly calls convention-correct). The corresponding test at `packages/core/tests/schema/frontmatterSchema.test.ts:48-57` asserts the exact field set, which is the right shape of assertion.

findings.title: The `--fix` path passes an explicit date stamp and the writer never reads a clock
findings.description: `formatDateProject()` is computed once per run and passed as the fourth argument to `updateFrontmatterField`, satisfying the slice's B1/B2 requirements and the "date passed as an explicit parameter (no inline clock)" constraint. The CLI test at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:120-127` pins the stamp format with `/^\d{8}$/`, which is a real behavioral assertion rather than a mock-shape assertion.

findings.title: The pre-existing `every schema requires docType, status, dateCreated, dateUpdated` test was correctly narrowed rather than deleted
findings.description: The original test iterated `Object.entries(FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS)`, which would have started failing the moment the three lifecycle-free docTypes were added. Narrowing the iteration to the explicit `EXPECTED_DOC_TYPES` list preserves the original invariant for canonical docTypes and adds a separate, explicit test for the new ones — rather than weakening the assertion to accommodate the new entries.

findings.title: `validate.ts` does not honor worktree resolution, unlike most sibling commands
findings.description: `resolveProjectWorktree` returns a `worktreeId` when CWD resolves to a worktree, but `validate.ts` destructures only `{ id }` and always validates `project.projectPath`. Sibling commands (`arch.ts:53`, `slice.ts:36`, `task.ts:50`, `plan.ts:43`) route filesystem operations through `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)`. This may well be intentional — the slice design says the command resolves "the configured document root" and `cf check` itself is worktree-agnostic — but it is an undocumented asymmetry for a command whose primary consumer is a git pre-commit hook, where the CWD is very often a worktree root. Worth either routing through `resolveOperationPath` or stating explicitly in the help text that validation always targets the main project root.
